questions.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch the graph of  $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{4})+\pi :$   

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14252450/assets/42eb38a11d9d63e05c0078bae4c052566b3162571e8563f22cd52ae31bc6dbd7.png)

The domain of   $\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{4})+\pi $ is $(-\infty ,\infty ).$  

Now, substituting $x=4$ directly into the limit, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{4})+\pi ) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1)+\pi ) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+\pi ) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{4}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's sketch the graph of $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x+3):$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14252450/assets/bb49c052cabe12e8869270ab61b1de9e7f45b6acd6eaa9bc0d4c6892446a7cb6.png)

The domain of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x+3)$ is $(-\infty ,\infty ).$ Moreover, from the graph, we see that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x+3)=\frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,\infty }(10\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x+3))=(10\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})=5\pi .
$$

The domain of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3x)$ is $(-\infty ,\infty ).$

Now, substituting $x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ directly into the limit, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}cos\,(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3x)) & =cos\,(arctan\,(3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})) \\  & =cos\,(arctan\,(\sqrt{3})) \\  & =cos\,(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
